# Column bounds and the coarse bimodule generated by one normal coordinate over the others

## Current assessment

[Selected decision](#decision-reviewed)

## Statement

Let \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)\) be bounded normal generators of a finite von Neumann algebra \((M,\tau)\) with faithful normal probability trace, satisfying the [actual starred ACSY condition](../tasks/Yin_T_F0011_v1.md#contract).
Fix \(i\), let \(\mathcal P=\mathbb C\langle X,X^*\rangle\) and write \(\delta=\delta_i\) for the unique coordinate derivation, \(\xi=\delta^*(1\otimes1)\) for its actual vacuum, and \(E=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\tau)\delta\) for the canonical right slice on \(\mathcal P\).
Inner products are linear in the second variable.
Put \(N=W^*(X_j:j\ne i)\), with \(N=\mathbb C1\) if \(d=1\), and let \(\mathbb E_N\) be the trace-preserving conditional expectation and its \(L^2\) extension.
Set \(x=X_i-\mathbb E_N X_i\), \(\mathcal V=\operatorname{span}NxN\), \(H_x=\overline{\mathcal V}^{\,2}\subset L^2(M)\ominus L^2(N)\).

**Projected columns and the first layer.**
For every \(p\in\mathcal P\),
\[
                    \mathbb E_N(Ep)=\mathbb E_N(p\xi^*).
 \tag{1}
\]
On the entire subspace of bounded elements \(N+\mathcal V\), define \(Ey=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\tau)\bar\delta y\) using the closed derivation.
These vectors belong to its domain and satisfy \(Ey=\mathbb E_N(y\xi^*)\).
For any finite column \(p_k\in\mathcal P\),
\[
 \sum_k\|\mathbb E_N(Ep_k)\|_2^2
 \le\tau\!\left(\xi^*\xi\sum_k p_k^*p_k\right)
 \le\|\xi\|_2^2\left\|\sum_kp_k^*p_k\right\|.
 \tag{2}
\]
For columns in \(N+\mathcal V\), (2) holds for the entire right slice.
Thus finiteness of the [full-core column cost](Yin_C_F0208_v1.md#statement) is equivalent to finiteness of that cost for \((I-\mathbb E_N)E\) on \(\mathcal P\).

**The cyclic bimodule.**
Let \(A=N\bar\otimes N^{\mathrm{op}}\) with product trace \(\tau_A\), and use \(L^2(A)\) as the coarse \(N\)-bimodule.
For \(q=\sum_j a_j\otimes b_j^{\mathrm{op}}\in N\odot N^{\mathrm{op}}\), write \(q x=\sum_j a_j x b_j\) and \(q1_A=q\in L^2(A)\).
There is a closed densely defined map \(T:H_x\to L^2(A)\), the closure of \(q x\mapsto q1_A\).
Its range is dense, and
\[
  H_x=\ker T\ \oplus\ H_{\rm c},\qquad
  W:H_{\rm c}\longrightarrow L^2(A)
 \tag{3}
\]
is a unitary bimodule identification given by the polar part of \(T\) on \(H_{\rm c}=(\ker T)^\perp\).
Every bounded \(N\)-bimodule operator from \(\ker T\) to \(L^2(A)\) is zero.
In particular every copy of a subbimodule of the coarse bimodule inside \(H_x\) is contained in \(H_{\rm c}\).

With \(p_{\rm c}\) the projection onto \(H_{\rm c}\), there is a positive faithful affiliated \(h\) in \(A\) such that
\[
 \begin{split}
 Wp_{\rm c}x&=h^{1/2},\qquad
 \tau_A(h)=\|p_{\rm c}x\|_2^2\le\|x\|_2^2,\\
 W P_{H_x}\xi&=h^{-1/2},\qquad
 \tau_A(h^{-1})=\|P_{H_x}\xi\|_2^2\le\|\xi\|_2^2 .
 \end{split}                                                     \tag{4}
\]
Here \(P_{H_x}\xi\in H_{\rm c}\).
In particular the contribution of \(p_{\rm c}x\) to \(\|q x\|_2^2\) is exactly \(\tau_A(h q^*q)\).
The density in (4) is a density on the tensor product \(A\) for this cyclic bimodule.

**An obstruction to unitary conjugation.**
The coordinate \(x\) cannot belong to the closed span of vectors \(v\in L^2(M)\) for which \(bv=va\) with possibly different diffuse unitaries \(a,b\in N\) depending on \(v\).
In particular, if \(N\) is diffuse, \(x\) cannot belong to the \(L^2\)-closed span of the unitaries normalizing \(N\).
Consequently the normalizer of such an \(N\) cannot generate \(M\).

## Argument

### The closed derivation on the omitted-coordinate algebra

By the [normal starred phase theorem](Yin_C_F0076_v1.md#statement), \(\delta\) is closable and kills each omitted coordinate and its adjoint on the represented core.
The graph of \(\bar\delta\) in \(L^2(M)\oplus(L^2(M)\otimes_2L^2(M))\) is invariant under simultaneous left and right multiplication by the omitted star polynomials, with the outer actions on the tensor component.
Indeed the core Leibniz identity with an omitted polynomial passes to its graph closure by bounded multiplication.
The adjoint polynomials also act, so the graph projection commutes with those multipliers.
Normality of the actions gives commutation with all the corresponding \(N\)-multipliers, by the [graph argument for a diffuse omitted coordinate](Yin_C_F0202_v1.md#the-diffuse-coordinate-and-the-graph-of-the-derivation) applied to the whole omitted generating set.
In particular \(N\) is in the domain with zero derivative, since \((1,0)\) is in the graph.
It follows that \(\bar\delta x=1\otimes1\) and
\[
            \bar\delta\left(\sum_j a_j x b_j\right)=\sum_j a_j\otimes b_j
              \qquad (a_j,b_j\in N).
 \tag{5}
\]
This proves independence of the tensor from the chosen representation of the left side.
The bimodule property of conditional expectation gives \(\mathbb E_N(a x b)=0\), proving the stated orthogonality.

For any bounded \(p\) in the domain of \(\bar\delta\), put \(Ep=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\tau)\bar\delta p\).
For \(t\in N\), the established left graph action and the actual vacuum pairing yield
\[
 \langle t,Ep\rangle
  =\langle t\otimes1,\bar\delta p\rangle
  =\langle1\otimes1,\bar\delta(t^*p)\rangle
  =\langle\xi,t^*p\rangle
  =\langle t,p\xi^*\rangle .
\]
The adjoint pairing extends from the original core to the graph closure by continuity.
The last equality uses tracial cyclicity with the \(L^2\) factor \(\xi^*\).
Testing every \(t\in N\) proves (1), including for \(p\in N+\mathcal V\).
In the latter case slicing (5) gives \(Ep=\sum_j a_j\tau(b_j)\in N\) for the \(\mathcal V\)-part, while the \(N\)-part has slice zero.
For every finite column, \(L^2\)-contractivity of \(\mathbb E_N\) bounds the sum of squared projected norms by \(\sum_k\|p_k\xi^*\|_2^2=\tau(\xi^*\xi\sum_kp_k^*p_k)\).
This proves (2).
On the entire original core the squared norms of the projected and complementary slices add for each family, proving the equivalence of finiteness.

### Polar decomposition and the integrable inverse density

Embed \(L^2(N)\otimes_2L^2(N)\) as a closed subspace of the original coarse target.
Identify it unitarily with \(L^2(A)\) by \(a\otimes b\mapsto a\otimes b^{\mathrm{op}}\) on bounded tensors.
Tracial cyclicity on the second factor proves the Hilbert isometry with this complex-linear convention.
The outer actions \(a\eta b\) correspond to left multiplication by \(a\otimes b^{\mathrm{op}}\).
Thus (5) is \(q x\mapsto q1_A\).
Its restriction on \(\mathcal V\) is closable from \(H_x\) into this target by closability of the original derivation, and its range contains \(N\odot N^{\mathrm{op}}\), dense in \(L^2(A)\).
Take its indicated closure \(T\).
It is not necessary to identify the domain of \(T\) with the intersection of \(H_x\) and the full derivation domain.

The graph of \(T\) is invariant under the left and right \(N\) actions and their adjoints by (5) on its defining core.
For each unitary in either action it is therefore invariant also under the inverse, giving intertwining with equality on the domains.
Uniqueness of polar decomposition of a closed operator gives a partial isometry \(W\) intertwining these actions, and the spectral projections of \(|T^*|\) commute with them on \(L^2(A)\).
The initial space of \(W\) is \(H_{\rm c}\), and its final space is all of \(L^2(A)\) by dense range.
This proves (3) and that the projection \(p_{\rm c}\) commutes with both actions.

On \(L^2(A)\) the two outer actions generate the left regular algebra of \(A\).
Its commutant is right multiplication by \(A\) by the [standard tracial representation theorem](../audits/literature/AP18/Yin_U002.md#ap18-u002).
Since \(|T^*|\) is positive and injective, its spectral projections are the right spectral projections of a positive affiliated \(d\) in \(A\) with full support.
In particular \(|T^*|\) is right multiplication by \(d\) on its natural domain, as follows by bounded spectral truncation.
For the polar identities \(T=|T^*|W,\ T^*=W^*|T^*|\), extend \(W\) by zero on \(\ker T\).

The original actual vacuum gives \(\langle1_A,Tv\rangle=\langle\xi,v\rangle\) for \(v\in\mathcal V\) by (5).
Thus \(1_A\in\operatorname{Dom}T^*\) with \(T^*1_A=P_{H_x}\xi\).
It follows that \(1_A\in\operatorname{Dom}|T^*|\), \(d=|T^*|1_A\in L^2(A)\), and \(W P_{H_x}\xi=d\).
Also \(x\in\operatorname{Dom}T,\ Tx=1_A\) and \(T=|T^*|W\), so \(W x\) lies in \(\operatorname{Dom}|T^*|\) and \((W x)d=1_A\).
Cutting on the right by \(1_{[1/m,m]}(d)\) identifies \((W x)1_{[1/m,m]}(d)=d^{-1}1_{[1/m,m]}(d)\).
Full support and \(W x\in L^2(A)\) then give \(d^{-1}\in L^2(A)\) and \(W x=d^{-1}\).
Taking \(h=d^{-2}\) proves (4) in the stated order.
For \(q\in N\odot N^{\mathrm{op}}\), the regular component of \(q x\) is carried to \(q h^{1/2}\), whose squared norm is \(\tau_A(h q^*q)\).

### The kernel contains no coarse subrepresentation

Let \(J:\ker T\to L^2(A)\) be a bounded bimodule intertwiner and extend it by zero on \(H_{\rm c}\).
For \(y\in\ker T\), the graph core property supplies \(q_n\in N\odot N^{\mathrm{op}}\) with \(q_n x\to y\) and \(q_n1_A\to0\) in their Hilbert spaces.
Intertwining gives \(q_n(Jx)\to Jy\).
Set \(e_m=1_{[0,m]}(|Jx|)\in A\) using the tracial \(L^2(A)\) realization.
Then \(Jx\,e_m\) is bounded, so
\[
       \|q_n(Jx)e_m\|_2
       \le \|q_n1_A\|_2\,\|Jx\,e_m\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.
\]
It follows that \((Jy)e_m=0\) for all \(m\), hence \(Jy=0\) since \(e_m\uparrow1\).
Thus \(J=0\).
If a closed subbimodule of \(H_x\) embeds isometrically into the coarse bimodule, its orthogonal projection commutes with the bimodule actions.
Composing that projection with the embedding and applying the just proved vanishing on \(\ker T\) shows that the subbimodule lies in \(H_{\rm c}\).
This accounts for the whole coarse summand in the cyclic space generated by \(x\).

### Intertwining vectors and normalizers

Let \(p\) be the orthogonal projection of \(L^2(M)\) onto \(H_{\rm c}\).
This subspace reduces the left and right \(N\) actions.
If \(bv=va\) for diffuse unitaries \(a,b\in N\), the image of \(pv\) under the coarse unitary \(W\) therefore satisfies the same equation in the coarse bimodule.
There is no nonzero such vector.
Indeed the spectral measure of left \(b\) and right \(a\) on any elementary tensor is the product of two measures absolutely continuous with respect to their respective marginal trace spectral laws.
The two laws are diffuse, so that product gives zero mass to the diagonal of the circle squared by Fubini.
The diagonal joint spectral projection consequently kills every elementary tensor and then their closed span.
The equation \(b\eta=\eta a\) puts \(\eta\) in its range by the joint spectral theorem.
This proves \(pv=0\).
But \(p x\ne0\) by (4) and full support, which excludes the claimed closed span.

If \(N\) is diffuse choose a Haar unitary \(a\in N\), for example by successive equal-trace dyadic refinements in a diffuse abelian subalgebra.
For each unitary normalizer \(u\) take \(b=uau^*\in N\), which is also diffuse and satisfies \(bu=ua\).
Thus \(p\) kills every normalizer.
Their linear span is a unital star algebra, so if they generated \(M\) as a von Neumann algebra their span would be \(L^2\)-dense, contradicting \(p x\ne0\).

## Scope

The affiliated density \(h\) in (4) describes the coarse part of \(NxN\).
The [optimal normal state density for the full column estimate](Yin_C_F0211_v1.md#statement) acts in \(M\) and requires a finite full-core column cost.
Formula (2) supplies a bound for every mixed word after projection and a full bound for one unstarred occurrence with arbitrary omitted coefficients.
Multiple occurrences and the unprojected slice on the complete star-polynomial core remain the unresolved part of the [normal implication](../tasks/Yin_T_F0011_v1.md#contract).
